title: Meet Windows GTX 1080 timing targets after scene repairs
requires: Physical Windows GTX 1080, accepted scene repairs and complete retained F8-78 capture
scope: Post-F8 performance follow-up authorized on 2026-11-03. Optimize measured Windows GPU execution, submission, data movement and required completion waits after scene-quality corrections. Start from a fresh exact-source baseline and retain F8-78 history. Coordinate overlapping shared work through the existing locks. Preserve repaired physical semantics and all one-step, spatial and solver-work limits.
acceptance: Publish exact-source before/after profiles attributing CPU, required completion waits and native GPU costs. Retain all normal samples and stalls with device/toolchain and installed artifact provenance.

Pass the full registered Windows Release suite, ownership/completion regressions, affected portable/reference checks, relocated SDK and installed Gallery checks. Preserve the accepted F9 scene-quality improvements with independent physical checks.

Complete all 30 public cases, all 12 physical scenarios and physical/work/recovery assertions in both modes. Reproduce all five workloads using frozen counts, 600 warmup and 7200 measured ticks and zero failed ticks.

Meet the original targets in every workload/mode with physics p95 at most 10 ms, frame p95 at most 16.666666666666668 ms and simulated/wall ratio at least 0.99. Pass all five canonical negative controls from a passing unmodified baseline.

Preserve one 1/60-second advance, one spatial publication and independent iteration/dispatch/submission/readback/synchronization ceilings. Retain workload size, measurement boundaries, timeouts and capability coverage.
Publish raw evidence and exact source/tree, driver/SDK/manifest hashes, protected-closure classification and remaining limitations for F9-08 qualification planning.
